measurement.theFirstTwoAreCarried_theThirdIsNot: I traced each of the three to source. mustNot[0] comes from file 03 line 61-62's 'without logging the value'. mustNot[1] comes from the V1 law the artifact carries at lines 45-47, 'the value is excluded from PlanId, evidence digest, diagnostics, and support bundles'. mustNot[2] has no source: the strings 'outside the host broker' and 'store or retrieve' do not occur anywhere in file 03. It is the only element of the proposed remainder with no carrier.
measurement.theGoverningFileDeniesTheProperty: File 03's 'Preserved confinement honesty' section, lines 129-135, states: 'A child process is fault containment, not a sandbox… Otherwise the component is disclosed trusted code in the TCB. Host brokers used voluntarily by an unconstrained same-user process do not create confinement.' A rule that the broker must not LET a component reach credentials outside it asserts precisely the containment that sentence withholds from the default configuration.
measurement.theArtifactCarriesTheSameWarningInItsOwn: This is what makes it a defect rather than a debatable reading. Among the 23 lines the artifact carries verbatim is 'read-set and confinement enforcement, not handle terminology.' — file 03's warning that naming something a handle does not deliver confinement. The artifact reproduces that sentence and then, three keys later, writes a confinement obligation with no enforcement behind it.
measurement.itContradictsTheArtifactsOwnTwiceStatedL: authorityClaim says the artifact 'does not mint platform guarantees', and whatThisDoesNotDo repeats 'Does not mint platform guarantees or threat-model findings.' A broker that cannot be bypassed is a platform guarantee. The artifact also correctly reserves the 'platform threat model' as NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED at evidenceRemainder — so it withholds the evidence that would justify the claim while making the claim.
measurement.aLawfulBasisForTheSCOPEExistsAndIsNotCit: I looked for a carrier before calling this minted, and there is one for the subject matter though not for the phrasing: the live host-effect-authorization.v8 routes 'keychain → DR-108, still deferred, unexercisable'. So component credential access is genuinely this row's question. The artifact never cites that routing, so the one available basis for mustNot[2]'s scope is absent from recordedInputs.

shouldFix.whyShouldFixAndNotBlocker: Because the artifact's correct position is stated elsewhere and governs. authorityClaim and whatThisDoesNotDo both disclaim platform guarantees, evidenceRemainder reserves the threat model, and proposedBroker.standing marks the whole object 'PROPOSED remainder. Exact API reserved.' Read against those, mustNot[2] is most charitably an interface constraint — the sanctioned design must offer components no side path to credential storage — which is a legitimate thing for this row to say and does not contradict confinement honesty. Nothing is orphaned and no authority is exported. But the sentence as written does not say that, and in a security contract the difference between 'the interface offers no such path' and 'a component cannot take one' is the whole question.
shouldFix.whyItIsNotMerelyAdvisory: Three reasons. First, it is the single unsourced element in an artifact whose entire method is carriage — every other normative statement traces to file 03, file 02 line 184, the DR-108 row, or D-002, and this one traces nowhere. Second, it is exactly the failure mode this row's governing text was written to prevent: file 03 spends two separate passages warning that handle terminology and voluntary brokers do not produce confinement, and both passages are about credentials. Third, a later successor or the threat-model author would reasonably read mustNot as settled design constraints and inherit an unearned containment assumption into the very artifact — the platform threat model — that exists to test it.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Disambiguate in one clause and cite the carrier. For example: the sanctioned interface exposes no component-side credential store or retrieve path; whether a component can nonetheless reach credentials outside the broker is a confinement question governed by file 03's Preserved confinement honesty and is not resolved here. Adding host-effect-authorization.v8's 'keychain → DR-108, still deferred, unexercisable' routing to recordedInputs would give the scope its source.

advisories.title: 'D-096 (A) deferral' mischaracterizes the mechanism — (A) is an owner grant, not a deferral
advisories.detail: The subject reads 'This statement is not a D-096 (A) deferral of DR-108.' D-096 defines (A) as 'an applicable owner grant covering every named role for the candidate being recorded', paired with (B) separately reviewed owner-recording mechanics, and adds 'A mechanics entry alone never grants.' D-097 then records 'Adopt nothing as D-096 (A). D-096 (A) remains unsatisfied' and reserves it to an express user grant. So (A) is a grant limb, not a deferral instrument.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The sentence is a disclaimer, and it errs toward disclaiming more than required — it gives nothing away and grants nothing. The artifact's related factual claim is separately correct: recordedInputs states 'D-096 (A) is unsatisfied', which I verified against D-097's live text. The substance of sliceStanding is also right: DR-108 is slice-conditional per COORDINATOR-DECISIONS lines 253-255, and D-002 already gave it the explicit deferral disposition that rule requires — 'DR-108 (no credential-requiring features in slice 1)'.
advisories.suggestedFix: Say what is meant: this statement is not an owner-recording act and does not supply the express grant D-096 (A) requires.

advisories.title: 'a sealed DR-108' applies artifact vocabulary to a register row
advisories.detail: The text reads 'Absence of a sealed DR-108 does not block the slice's non-credential path.' In this corpus rows receive dispositions — OPEN, SATISFIED, DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED — while sealing is a property of artifacts, which is why this artifact carries its own sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL. A row is not sealed or unsealed.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The proposition is true under any reasonable reading and is independently supported twice: the row's own seventh cell says 'Hard blocker only for features requiring stored credentials', and D-002 deferred DR-108 out of slice 1 explicitly. Only the noun is wrong.
advisories.suggestedFix: 'Absence of a SATISFIED DR-108', or 'the row's OPEN status'.

verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 3 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. REJECT.
verdictStatement: This is a disciplined extraction and it very nearly clears. Its method is carriage, and the carriage is exact: 23 lines byte-identical to file 03 lines 41-63, the register row byte-identical to line 290 across all seven cells with a uniquely resolving anchor, and file 02's handle line byte-identical and correctly located in the section DR-125 governs. It is the first artifact I have measured in this corpus with no stale pin at all — all four recorded digests are live at the current HEAD. It declines everything the dispatch warned about: no vendor API, no cipher or KDF, no file mode or path, no owner grant, no invented successor artifact, no conflation of the row with the like-named coordinator decision, and no disposition of the row, since its slice statements restate D-002's existing deferral and the register's own slice-conditional rule rather than performing one. Where it reserves, it reserves to real rows — SDK APIs to DR-125, the evidence remainder to the row's own fifth-cell items in the row's own words, marked NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED. What fails is one clause. Of the three broker prohibitions, two trace cleanly to file 03; the third — that the broker must not let a component store or retrieve credentials outside it — traces nowhere, and neither 'outside the host broker' nor 'store or retrieve' appears in the governing file. Worse than unsourced, it is stated in enforcement language that file 03 specifically withholds: 'Host brokers used voluntarily by an unconstrained same-user process do not create confinement.' The artifact carries, in its own bytes and verbatim, the sibling warning that confidentiality 'requires actual read-set and confinement enforcement, not handle terminology' — and then writes a containment obligation with no enforcement behind it, in a document that twice promises it does not mint platform guarantees and that correctly reserves the very threat model which would have to establish this one. It is not a blocker: the artifact's disclaimers govern, the object is marked PROPOSED with the API reserved, and the charitable reading — that the sanctioned interface offers components no credential path — is both lawful and probably intended. But in a credential contract the gap between 'the interface offers no such path' and 'a component cannot take one' is the entire subject, and this row exists because that gap has to be closed with evidence rather than wording. One disambiguating clause, plus a citation of the live 'keychain → DR-108, still deferred, unexercisable' routing that would give the clause its scope, and this is a 0/0 artifact.

coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-108 stays OPEN at file 08 line 290; I did not touch file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, marked nothing SATISFIED, authorized no implementation, invented no keychain/file/broker API, and minted no D-096 (A) grant — that limb remains unsatisfied per D-097 and reserved to an express user act, and nothing here substitutes for it. Five things to weigh. First, the single finding is one clause in a nine-word list and the repair needs no decision: scope mustNot[2] to the sanctioned interface, or drop it, and the artifact is clean. Second, the finding is worth taking seriously despite its size because of what this row is — file 03 devotes two separate passages to warning that handles and voluntary brokers do not produce confinement, and an unearned containment assumption inherited into the platform threat model is precisely the failure those passages exist to prevent. Third, the artifact is otherwise the cleanest first-version candidate I have reviewed here: exact carriage, fully live pins, correct standing on every axis, and a scrupulous refusal to decide what it does not own. Fourth, a small correction the coordinator may want in a v2 regardless of the finding: the subject calls D-096 (A) a 'deferral' when D-096 and D-097 define it as an owner grant — the disclaimer is harmless and errs safe, but the vocabulary should not propagate. Fifth, no Codex verdict for this subject existed on disk during my review, so this lane is uncorrelated by circumstance as well as by instruction.
